newsItems.title: Djokovic Outlasts Auger-Aliassime in Longest Wimbledon Quarter-Final Ever
newsItems.excerpt: Novak Djokovic wrote another chapter into Wimbledon folklore on Tuesday night, July 7, surviving the longest men's quarter-final in tournament history to defeat third seed Felix Auger-Aliassime 7-6 (12-10), 3-6, 6-3, 6-7 (4-7), 7-6 (10-4) after five hours and 15 minutes on Centre Court. The 39-year-old seven-time champion, who received treatment for a left calf problem in the opening set and argued with officials over the timing of the roof closure, became the oldest men's semi-finalist at SW19 in 50 years and extended his all-time record to 107 Wimbledon match wins and a 15th semi-final appearance. Auger-Aliassime pushed Djokovic to the brink in a match where the scoreline stayed level throughout, but the Serb barely missed in the deciding 10-point tie-break to finish six minutes before the 11pm curfew. Djokovic will face defending champion Jannik Sinner in Friday's semi-final — a rematch of last year's Wimbledon last four and January's five-set Australian Open classic — as he pursues a 25th Grand Slam title. Sinner advanced earlier by beating Jan-Lennard Struff 7-5, 7-6 (7-4), 6-3, while Alexander Zverev completed a four-set win over Jiri Lehecka to set up a quarter-final against Taylor Fritz on Wednesday.

newsItems.title: Syafiq Kamal Ends Seven-Year Wait with PSA Mumbai Challenger Title
newsItems.excerpt: Malaysia's Mohammad Syafiq Kamal produced one of the comebacks of the early summer squash season at the HCL-SRFI PSA Challenger Tour Mumbai 2026, fighting back from two games down to defeat Egypt's second seed Yassin Shohdy 6-11, 9-11, 11-8, 14-12, 11-8 in a gripping men's final at the Juhu Gymkhana Club. The victory ended a seven-year drought since Syafiq's last PSA crown at the SRAM PSA 1 in Bukit Jalil in 2019 and arrived with extra significance after the Squash Racquets Association of Malaysia confirmed his place in the national squad for the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games from September 19 to October 4. Shohdy had controlled the opening two games and looked poised to add to his ACE Challenger triumph in Kerteh, but Syafiq raised his intensity to force a decider and closed with an 11-8 fifth-game win. The women's final delivered equal drama as India's Tanvi Khanna, the world No. 74 and third seed, recovered from 0-2 down to beat Egyptian second seed Farida Walid 8-11, 2-11, 12-10, 11-9, 11-7 for her fifth PSA title in 11 final appearances. The five-day event featured 48 professionals from 15 countries and underscored India's growing profile on the global PSA calendar.

newsItems.title: Malaysia Pioneers AI Line Review at Junior Badminton Tournament
newsItems.excerpt: The Badminton Association of Malaysia broke new ground on July 8 by becoming the first badminton body in the region to introduce an AI-powered Instant Review System at a domestic junior event during the AFFIN 100PLUS Junior Elite Tour Finals 2026 in Kuala Lumpur. Developed by Revealtek Sdn Bhd and approved by the BWF, the system uses artificial intelligence and 480fps cameras to review line-call challenges and deliver decisions within seconds, giving young players exposure to international-standard officiating at a formative stage of their careers. BAM said the deployment enhances transparency and fairness while setting a benchmark for junior competition across Southeast Asia. Revealtek plans to roll out the technology at the Singapore International Challenge in August and is targeting a pilot launch of its Electronic Line Calls system in September. The innovation arrives as the professional circuit turns toward the DAIHATSU Japan Open starting July 14 at the Tokyo Metropolitan Gymnasium, where Malaysia's reshuffled men's doubles pair of Man Wei Chong and Olympic bronze medallist Soh Wooi Yik will make their tournament debut under national coach Herry IP's new combination experiments.

newsItems.title: Singapore Open Positions Asia's Pickleball Hub for Bigger Events
newsItems.excerpt: With the PPA Asia 500 Singapore Open three weeks away, the region's pickleball ecosystem is building toward its most significant staging yet at The Sports Arina @ Expo from July 23 to 26. The $70,000 event — the sixth of 10 stops on the 2026 PPA Tour Asia calendar — follows April's PPA Asia 125 at PickleSlam and arrives as Malaysia's top-ranked Jimmy Liong voices confidence that Singapore will soon host even larger professional tournaments. "Asia is definitely growing, and Singapore as well," Liong said ahead of the event. "I met a few partners of PPA in Singapore, and I believe it's going to happen sooner or later." United Pickleball Association Asia managing director Kimberly Koh framed the Singapore Open as a deliberate step in a progression from entry-level events through mid-tier competitions to flagship stops such as the $1.1 million Hong Kong Slam in October. Hong Kit Wong carries momentum into the stretch after capturing his third PPA Tour Asia singles title at the Sansan Tokyo Open without dropping a game, while the global tour simultaneously expands into Europe with the PPA Italy 125 in Portorož, Slovenia, July 22–26 and domestic stops in Melbourne and Macon through mid-July.
